level_note: Proposed baseline tags. D1 means the smallest familiar demand within each type; SYNTHESIZE still requires a short dependent chain. Tags require non-author checking; this bank is not calibrated to JEE Main exam difficulty.

questions.stem: Block A (2 kg) pushes block B (3 kg) with 8 N to the right. What contact force does B exert on A?

options.text: 8 N to the right.
12 N to the left.
8 N to the left.

questions.expected_reason: Apply the third law to the specified interaction: equal magnitude 8 N, opposite direction left, received by A. The mass ratio does not scale this pair.
questions.type_rationale: Uses a known law directly on a specified interaction.

A.possible_interpretation: May preserve magnitude without reversing direction.

B.possible_interpretation: May multiply the force by the 3/2 mass ratio.

C.possible_interpretation: May replace either member of a force pair with the combined sum.

questions.stem: A (2 kg, on the left) and B (3 kg, on the right) touch on a frictionless horizontal table. A 15 N horizontal push acts rightward on A and they remain in contact. What contact force does B exert on A?

options.text: 15 N to the left.
6 N to the left.
9 N to the left.

questions.expected_reason: Choose a route: for A+B, a=15/(2+3)=3 m/s² right. Isolate B: A's contact force on B=3×3=9 N right. The reciprocal force on A is 9 N left. An equivalent consistent route is acceptable.
questions.type_rationale: Must choose and connect a short dependent route through the combined system and an individual body; no route or intermediate acceleration is given.

A.possible_interpretation: May equate the contact force to the full external push.

B.possible_interpretation: May report A's net force, 2×3=6 N, as the contact force.

D.possible_interpretation: May treat an internal force as individually zero because the pair cancels in a combined sum.

questions.stem: On block B, block A exerts 6 N to the right and the table exerts 2 N of friction to the left. Right is positive. Which equation translates these words into the net horizontal force on B?

options.text: F_net,x = (6 + 2) N.
F_net,x = (6 - 2) N.
F_net,x = (2 - 6) N.

questions.expected_reason: Translate the supplied directions and axis: +6 N from A and -2 N from the table. B's reciprocal force on A does not belong in B's force sum.
questions.type_rationale: Translates a verbal description into a signed equation; forces and positive direction are supplied.

A.possible_interpretation: May add magnitudes without representing direction.

C.possible_interpretation: May reverse the specified positive direction.

D.possible_interpretation: May add B's force on A to the forces received by B.

questions.stem: Touching blocks A (4 kg) and B (6 kg) move together on a frictionless horizontal table. A 20 N horizontal push acts on A. To find their common acceleration without first finding the contact force, which system and force choice is valid?

options.text: Choose A+B; use 20 N as the net horizontal external force and 10 kg as the mass.
Choose A alone; use 20 N as its net horizontal force and 4 kg as the mass.
Choose A+B; use 0 N because the contact pair cancels.
Choose B alone; use 20 N as its net horizontal force and 6 kg as the mass.

questions.expected_reason: Choose both blocks as the system. Their mutual contact forces are internal; the external horizontal push is 20 N and the system mass is 4+6=10 kg.
questions.type_rationale: Selects a system and strategy among plausible alternatives; calculation is not requested.

B.possible_interpretation: May ignore B's contact force when isolating A.

C.possible_interpretation: May extend cancellation of internal forces to the external push.

D.possible_interpretation: May assign the push on A directly to B.

questions.stem: Two touching blocks can speed up under an external push even though their mutual contact forces are equal and opposite. Which explanation resolves this?

options.text: The pair cancels on each block, so the external push does all the accelerating.
Each contact force has a different receiver; the net force on each block must be considered separately.
Acceleration temporarily makes the third law invalid.
The contact forces become unequal whenever the blocks accelerate.

questions.expected_reason: Equal and opposite contact forces have different receivers. They are not two forces to cancel in the force sum for either individual block; the combined system can accelerate under a net external push.
questions.type_rationale: Explains why an apparently contradictory result is consistent with the law.

A.possible_interpretation: May cancel forces belonging to different individual force diagrams.

C.possible_interpretation: May restrict the third law to unaccelerated situations.

D.possible_interpretation: May confuse unequal net forces with unequal mutual contact forces.

questions.stem: Blocks A (2 kg) and B (3 kg) touch. Calibrated contact-force measurements are listed below. Which conclusion is supported by these measurements?

options.text: In all three trials the contact-force magnitudes matched even though the masses differed.
The heavier block always exerted more force.
The blocks must have been stationary in all three trials.
These three measurements prove the law for every possible interaction.

questions.expected_reason: Use the explicit evidence: 4=4, 7=7 and 5=5 N with unequal masses. The table supports the stated conclusion for these trials; it supplies no motion measurements and is not a universal proof.
questions.type_rationale: Selects and defends a conclusion constrained by explicit measurement evidence, rather than merely reciting a law.

B.possible_interpretation: May prefer a mass-based claim over the listed equal measurements.

C.possible_interpretation: May infer rest from the reciprocal contact pair alone.

D.possible_interpretation: May treat three supporting trials as proof for every possible case.

questions.stem: Which statement must be true for a Newton's third-law force pair?

options.text: The two forces act on the same object.
The heavier object exerts the larger force.
The forces have equal magnitudes, opposite directions and different receivers.
The reaction starts after the action ends.

questions.expected_reason: Recall the defining properties of a third-law pair: reciprocal interactions, equal magnitude, opposite direction, different receiving objects, simultaneous.
questions.type_rationale: Recalls defining properties of a law; no calculation or strategy choice is required.

A.possible_interpretation: May place both interaction forces on one receiving object.

B.possible_interpretation: May think unequal masses imply unequal interaction forces.

D.possible_interpretation: May interpret reaction as a later event.
